name: Modge
summary: Desktop time tracking and workforce analytics for remote and hybrid teams: automatic hours, app and URL classification, shift adherence, leave, payroll-ready timesheets and Stripe invoicing. 14-day trial, no card.
best_for: desk-bound remote or hybrid teams of a few to a few hundred people who want time tracking, app classification, shift adherence, leave and payroll-ready timesheets in one seat priced between $4 and $7 a month, and who are happy to run screenshots as an opt-in rather than a default
skip_if: you need SSO or a SOC 2 report today, both are marked soon; your people work in the field, since the agent is desktop-only with no mobile or GPS on the page; or your security team will not accept a compliance claim without a document
honest_knock: The numbers on Modge's own pages do not agree with each other. The homepage says trusted by 1,000+ teams, the affiliate page says 1,800+ teams, the pricing page says over 2,000 users; the pricing page also shows three star ratings, 4.6 from 1,500 reviews, 4.8 from 2,000 and 4.2 from 800, without naming a single platform they come from. None of that touches the product, but it is the kind of copy a buyer should not repeat in a business case. What does touch the product is the comparison table: SSO through SAML 2.0, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 9001 are all marked soon, and HIPAA compliant appears with no report behind it. If your security review needs a document today, there is none to hand over. The desktop agent is macOS and Windows only, and the pricing page mentions no mobile app or GPS, so field teams are out of scope.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-03 on modge.com/pricing, both billing toggles and the comparison table) Per-seat plans with a full-feature 14-day trial and no card. Basic is $5 per seat per month billed monthly or $4 billed annually: app and URL tracking with AI productivity classification, workforce dashboards, automatic time tracking with optional screenshots, timesheets, approvals and payroll exports, invoice creation, email and chat support. Pro is $7 monthly or $5.50 annually and adds shifts, scheduling and adherence, leave, breaks and overtime, client billing through Stripe, on-demand screenshots with 12-month retention, and custom roles, teams and project budgets. Premium, marked popular, is $9 monthly or $7 annually and adds automated project and task time tracking, workflow analysis, suspicious-activity and mouse-jiggler detection, burnout-risk and profitability insights, contract signing, 24-month screenshot retention and a dedicated account manager. Enterprise is custom, on annual billing with volume pricing, custom retention, customised onboarding and an SLA. Two add-ons are priced per seat: More Screenshots at $2 a month lifts capture from 18 to 60 an hour on Basic, Pro and Premium; Extended Data Retention at $2 a month or $1.67 annually keeps records for six years on every tier. The comparison table lists screenshot retention as 3 months on Basic, 12 on Pro and 24 on Premium, and marks SSO (SAML 2.0), SOC 2 Type II and ISO 9001 as soon.

compare_with.name: Hubstaff
compare_with.why: The obvious comparison. Hubstaff's annual column starts at $4.99 a seat with a two-seat minimum and its monthly column at $7; Modge starts at $4 annual or $5 monthly with no minimum on the page. Hubstaff has the longer record, a mobile app with GPS and a far larger integration list; Modge's pitch is shift adherence, leave policies and Stripe invoicing built into a cheaper seat, with screenshots off by default. Pick Hubstaff for field teams, Modge for desk-bound teams that also need rotas.
